title: C175E — Powertrain control module (PCM)
introduction:
This reference maps the PCM’s connections to engine and transmission circuits. I start with the connector identity and harness record, find the cavity label in the drawing, then read its complete assignment row. It works like an address book: finding the right address identifies the connection, but it does not prove that the electrical message is getting through.

The Function column separates sensor information, control outputs, supplies and returns. Configuration qualifiers matter wherever a cavity has alternative rows; keep each row’s wire and terminal information together. This guide identifies connections, not physical access, connector release, live probing or fault diagnosis. Physical viewing direction, the shading legend, gauge convention and Size/Used code definitions remain unspecified. The summary Pin Count disagrees with the drawing’s cavity count. Some repeated cavities combine a qualified row with an unqualified or overlapping alternative; the supplied table does not resolve their physical applicability. The count discrepancy and those assignment limitations remain unresolved; do not infer extra cavities or a definitive configuration from this reference.

edits.why: In this displayed view, the broad cavity field lies at the left, a separate rectangular cavity group sits at the right, and the outer housing projections extend farther right. These are drawing landmarks, not identified release mechanisms. Within each cavity group, labels increase from left to right across a row, with successive rows above. I use the printed labels to move between the illustration and table; the housing division makes an assumed continuous row especially easy to misread. Circle fill alone does not establish an assignment or electrical condition.

Read across from Cavity to Circuit Number, Color, Gauge, Function, Qualifier, Used and Terminal Part Number. The circuit identifier and function describe the connection; the qualifier determines the stated configuration. Repeated cavities can carry different wire, terminal or function information for different configurations, so do not combine cells from alternative rows or treat a blank qualifier as proof of universal applicability. Injector drivers and variable camshaft timing valve controls are outputs; throttle-position descriptions identify sensor signals. Supply, reference and return labels have separate roles. Preserve the fuse-or-circuit-breaker alternative in the supply description rather than choosing a protective device. These labels identify what to look up next in the matching circuit procedure; they do not establish test voltages, injector firing order or a failed component.
